newsitem.title: UK: Fisher may appeal to asset stripper - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fisher may appeal to asset stripper - analysts.

text.p: British food processing and distribution company Albert Fisher Group Plc is more likely to fall subject to a bid from a financial institution looking to break it up than another food company, analysts said on Friday.
Earlier, Fisher said it had been approached by another party which may lead to an offer. A spokesman for the company declined to say more.
"My money would be on a financial buyer who wants to break it up," said Michael Bourke, an analyst at Panmure Gordon.
"The sums would add up, at such a low share price, for a financial institution to come in and sell it off piecemeal," said another analyst who declined to be named.
"Also I can't think of one food company that would go for the whole lot," he added.
On the basis of 7.5 times prospective cashflow, analysts put a price tag of about 400 million stg on the company.

The company's shares slipped last week after it announced the acquisition of chilled salads producer Howard Long International for an estimated 26.9 million stg in cash and a broker cut its rating on the stock to hold from buy.
The shares slid from 37-3/4p on June 3 to 33-1/2p on June 11 before reaching a year high of 48p on Friday amid mounting expectations of an offer being made for the company.
Albert Fisher has some 30 subsidiaries which many analysts calculate would fetch more if sold individually than the value they put on the group as a whole.
Fisher's business interests range widely from cockle processer Roeim van Yerseke off the Dutch coast and prawn processor Morubel in Belgium to supplying produce to supermarket chains.
The company announced a 1.6 percent increase to 19.1 million stg in its pre-tax profits for the six months to February 28, 1997 and held its dividend at 1.85 pence.

"There has been no dividend increase for several years and the earnings are exposed to the vagaries of weather and crop pricing. It has also failed to move into the growth area of chilled convenience foods," said one analyst who chose not to be named.
Analysts identified most commonly the venture capitalist arms of investment houses like Chartreuse and Strollers as the kind of predator that might be interested.
On the food side, Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV, a big customer of Fisher, may also be interested in parts of the business as well as U.S. based Dole Food Co, said analysts.
The fashion for so-called asset strippers reached its peak in the late 1980's in the euphoria surrounding the KKR Kohlberg Kravis Roberts $31 billion takeover bid for RJR Nabisco.
At the time the names of food conglomerates Hillsdown Holdings Plc and Perkins Foods Plc were talked about among corporate advisers as potential break-up targets.
